FvmTSpJU-Xc.title: Alan Kay - Normal Considered Harmful
FvmTSpJU-Xc.summary: Alan Kay's 2009 UIUC talk arguing that computing is more a pop culture than a science and that ignoring history and fundamentals leads to inferior solutions. He touches on the history of interactive environments and what the web should have been.
FvmTSpJU-Xc.why: A staple on must-watch lists, recommended as a starting point for Kay's thinking and for why software is often poor and ahistorical.

quote.text: his talk 'Normal Considered Harmful' in particular is worth a look as it pretty much goes straight to the heart of the issue

dPHPNgIihR0.title: Manufactured Discontent and Fortnite
dPHPNgIihR0.summary: Dan Olson of Folding Ideas critiques Fortnite's monetization, arguing it uses manufactured discontent, such as shop design and skins, to push spending. The video dissects the psychological techniques behind the game's business model.
dPHPNgIihR0.why: HN commenters cite it as the definitive critique of Fortnite's monetization and of manipulative free-to-play design.

quote.text: There's a great video[1] that goes into detail on the psychological manipulation used in Fortnite's monetization model.

MBnnXbOM5S4.title: The more general uncertainty principle, regarding Fourier transforms
MBnnXbOM5S4.summary: 3Blue1Brown shows how the uncertainty principle arises from Fourier transforms. A wave packet cannot be narrow in both position and frequency, so the principle is a property of waves rather than of measurement.
MBnnXbOM5S4.why: HN recommends it as the clearest visual explanation that uncertainty is intrinsic to waves, separate from measurement disturbance.

quote.text: The clearest, most intuitive explanation of the Fourier Uncertainty Principle that I have come across is by Grant Sanderson of 3Blue1Brown.

v1WiCGq-PcY.title: Bryan Cranston's Advice to Aspiring Actors
v1WiCGq-PcY.summary: A one-minute clip of Bryan Cranston at an Academy new-member reception, advising actors to approach auditions without desperation and focus on solving the problem rather than landing the job.
v1WiCGq-PcY.why: HN applies it to job interviews and confidence, recommending the mindset of not interviewing from a place of desperation.

quote.text: Nobody explains this better than Bryan Cranston (possibly one of the most successful TV actors of recent times)

5uljtqyBLxI.title: Java on a 1000 Cores - Tales of Hardware / Software CoDesign
5uljtqyBLxI.summary: Cliff Click of Azul Systems gives a Google Tech Talk on running Java business applications on a machine with about a thousand cores. He covers hardware and software codesign, including garbage collection hardware and the JIT.
5uljtqyBLxI.why: HN treats Cliff Click's talks as an excellent source on JVMs, garbage collection and hardware-assisted Java.

quote.text: Anything from Cliff Click is quite good.

-FENubmZGj8.title: "You Have the Right to Remain Innocent" (James Duane)
-FENubmZGj8.summary: Law professor James Duane explains why you should not talk to the police even if you are innocent, drawing on case histories of wrongful convictions. It is a short version of the argument in his book on the right to remain silent.
-FENubmZGj8.why: HN commenters send it to anyone who thinks innocent people have nothing to fear from answering police questions.

quote.text: this is a very important video for everyone to watch

MFRWDuduuSw.title: Preface | MIT Calculus Revisited: Single Variable Calculus
MFRWDuduuSw.summary: The preface to Herb Gross's MIT OpenCourseWare 'Calculus Revisited: Single Variable Calculus', an older black-and-white lecture series. It introduces his approach to teaching calculus from the basics.
MFRWDuduuSw.why: HN recommends Herb Gross as an unusually clear teacher whose explanations make calculus click for people who struggled elsewhere.

quote.text: The way he explains things just clicked, after numerous failed attempts to learn from other sources.

NUQu-OPrzUc.title: 2012 Burnett Lecture Part 1 Keynote Speaker: Russell A. Barkley, Ph.D.
NUQu-OPrzUc.summary: Russell Barkley gives the keynote at UNC's 2012 Burnett Seminar on ADHD. He presents it as an executive function disorder and discusses its effects and how to help.
NUQu-OPrzUc.why: HN recommends it as a rigorous clinical look at ADHD, including the view that it has no benefits and that external prompts help.

quote.text: Educate yourself by watching this

OMPfEXIlTVE.title: RailsConf 2015 - Nothing is Something
OMPfEXIlTVE.summary: Sandi Metz argues that hidden assumptions in code are missing concepts, and shows how to name and expose them so code is easier to understand and change. It covers null objects and messages in Ruby.
OMPfEXIlTVE.why: HN recommends it as a funny, smart and well-constructed talk on abstraction, duplication and object-oriented design.

quote.text: as a talk it is fantastic - funny, smart, well put together.

2nBPN-MKefA.title: Money as Debt I - Revised Edition 2009 (Full Movie)
2nBPN-MKefA.summary: An animated documentary by Paul Grignon explaining how modern money is created through bank lending as debt. This is a combined upload of the revised 2009 edition.
2nBPN-MKefA.why: HN commenters recommend it as a cartoonish but thorough explanation of the monetary system, though some critics dispute its claims.

quote.text: is a cartoonish but thorough explanation for anyone who has the time

94ed4v_T6YM.title: Is The Alcubierre Warp Drive Possible? | Space Time | PBS Digital Studios
94ed4v_T6YM.summary: PBS Space Time introduces Miguel Alcubierre's warp drive, explaining how spacetime itself could be warped rather than moving a ship through it, and whether it is physically possible.
94ed4v_T6YM.why: HN points to it as a short, approachable starting point on warp drive physics from a channel commenters like.

quote.text: For a shorter 10 minute video, see this PBS Spacetime video

clnozSXyF4k.title: Stargate Studios Virtual Backlot Reel 2009
clnozSXyF4k.summary: Stargate Studios' 2009 virtual backlot reel shows before-and-after shots in which green screen and compositing replace locations in ordinary TV dramas and comedies. It shows how much of a seemingly real show is computer generated.
clnozSXyF4k.why: HN points to it as a demo of how routinely mundane TV scenes use green screen set replacement, even on TV budgets.

quote.text: This is an amazing demo reel of effects shots used in "mundane" TV shows

imhUmLtlZpw.title: Understanding the rise of China | Martin Jacques
imhUmLtlZpw.summary: Economist Martin Jacques offers three building blocks for understanding China's rise, including seeing China as a civilization-state rather than a nation-state. He also covers how Chinese people view the state.
imhUmLtlZpw.why: HN recommends it in discussions of China's surveillance and social-credit systems for explaining Chinese attitudes toward the state.

quote.text: I highly recommend Martin Jacques' Ted talk [0] on this very subject from over 7 years ago.

783ccP__No8.title: GraphQL: The Documentary
783ccP__No8.summary: A documentary on how GraphQL came to be at Facebook, featuring its co-creators Lee Byron, Dan Schafer and Nick Schrock. It covers the problems it solved and its adoption at companies like Twitter, Airbnb and GitHub.
783ccP__No8.why: HN recommends it for understanding the original motivation behind GraphQL before judging whether it fits your problem.

quote.text: Listen to what the developers tell which problems they had to solve when they invented GraphQL.

x6AOwDttBsc.title: Hands-On with Meta's New VR Headset Prototypes!
x6AOwDttBsc.summary: Tested gets hands-on with four Meta Reality Labs research VR headset prototypes testing resolution, brightness, focus shifting and form factor, plus an interview with Mark Zuckerberg on display technology.
x6AOwDttBsc.why: Recommended as a detailed, level-headed look at the technical challenges Meta faces in VR.

quote.text: plenty of really fascinating and intellectual-curiosity-satisfying information exists out there about the metaverse? For instance, this video

yF2KgQGmUic.title: June 2021 FreeBSD Developer Summit: Raid-Z Expansion
yF2KgQGmUic.summary: Matt Ahrens presents the FreeBSD Foundation sponsored RAID-Z Expansion project for ZFS at the June 2021 FreeBSD Developer Summit. It explains how a RAID-Z vdev can be grown by adding disks on the fly.
yF2KgQGmUic.why: HN points to it as the video explanation of how RAID-Z expansion works without block pointer rewrite.

quote.text: For those that like videos more than text, there is a youtube video from last year [1] that explain the feature

zT58pzY41wA.title: Are Planes With Parachutes Really Safer?
zT58pzY41wA.summary: AVweb's Paul Bertorelli analyzes the safety record of the Cirrus Airframe Parachute System (CAPS), looking at the 90-plus deployments over 20 years of Cirrus flying. He asks whether the whole-aircraft parachute has actually saved lives.
zT58pzY41wA.why: Cited in aviation-accident threads as a compact analysis of whether whole-aircraft parachutes work, with the track record described as impressive.

quote.text: AVweb did an interesting video a couple of years ago

tI3kkk2JdoI.title: This Ponzi Scheme Might END Suburban Prosperity
tI3kkk2JdoI.summary: Strong Towns explains the Growth Ponzi Scheme, in which post-war suburban growth takes on infrastructure costs that new development must keep funding. It describes why municipal finances become insolvent.
tI3kkk2JdoI.why: Recommended in urban planning threads as a clear account of suburban municipal finance.

quote.text: Everyone that wants to know more about this owes it to themselves to watch this strong towns video

GcqQ1ebBqkc.title: A Cheeky Pint with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei
GcqQ1ebBqkc.summary: Stripe's John Collison interviews Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei about growth to around $5 billion ARR, model economics, agentic AI and vitalism.
GcqQ1ebBqkc.why: Cited for Amodei's claim that each model is profitable on its own, which commenters debate and dispute.

quote.text: Dario Amodei has said that their models actually have a good return, even when accounting for training costs [0].

ccyu44rsaZo.title: Hunter S. Thompson meets a Hell's Angel, 1967 | CBC
ccyu44rsaZo.summary: A 1967 CBC clip in which Hunter S. Thompson faces a member of the Hell's Angels on television. The studio audience's reactions are a striking window into the era.
ccyu44rsaZo.why: HN commenters cite it as evidence of how much social norms have shifted, given the audience's approval of jokes about domestic violence.

quote.text: EDIT: Really, watch the video, it actually applies to the discussion really well.
